subject: VitriaHealth — assurance onramp, redline triage, and evidence tempo
messages:
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@vitriahealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@vitriahealth.com
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit + evidence tempo for VitriaHealth order form

Hi Grace / Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — Vitria is excited to move forward. Procurement asked that we align on the security exhibit language and the practical evidence tempo before we finalize the order form. Two quick asks to help us move through internal review: 

1) A proposed redline for the security exhibit that narrows inspection rights (sampled SOC 2 evidence + ephemeral pen-test access).
2) A short cadence for evidence handoff (SOC 2 artifact delivery windows and a 2-week pen-test notice or a carveout for staging access).

I've attached the list of Vitria's initial security questions to this thread.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is open to a bounded inspection approach (sampling + a narrow set of artifacts) and a stated pen-test notice window?

Thanks,
Alice Turner
Head of IT Compliance | VitriaHealth
alice.turner@vitriahealth.com
Attachments: Vitria_Security_Questions.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@vitriahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit + evidence tempo for VitriaHealth order form

Hi Alice — thanks for the doc and clear asks. Quick summary from our side and suggested next steps: 

- Redwood position (high level): we can accept a bounded inspection model for most customers: sampled SOC 2 artifacts, timeboxed pen-test access, and a mutual action plan that captures scheduling and redaction expectations. We prefer "sampled evidence + on-demand follow-up" language versus open-ended inspection.

- For SOC 2: we can commit to quarterly evidence bundles (extracts from the control matrix + auditor letter) and ad-hoc exports for specific assertions on a 10-business-day turnaround.

- For pen tests: we can offer a standard 14-day notice for a customer-run pen test against a staging environment; for scoped vendor-initiated tests we will require a signed MRA and a limited set of test types.

Next steps: Laura (legal) — can you propose concrete redline snippets that implement the "bounded inspection" approach? Ben — can you confirm whether the sales/order form can accept a 14-day pen-test notice and the quarterly evidence windows operationally?

I'll set a 30-minute triage call for Wednesday to go through the redline and mutual action plan.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Solution GTM | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Phone: +1-415-555-0192

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit + evidence tempo for VitriaHealth order form

Hi all — looping in proposed language.  I attached a short doc with three snippets (audit rights, evidence cadence, pen-test window) — called redline_snippets.docx.  Key calls: 

1) Audit scope: limited to SOC 2 assertions relevant to the service; customer may request specific artifacts for a sample of controls no more than twice per 12 months unless mutually agreed.

2) Evidence tempo: quarterly delivery of SOC 2-derived artifacts (control matrix excerpts and auditor attestation) with a 10-business-day SLA for follow-up requests that are reasonable in scope.

3) Pen test: 14-calendar-day notice for a customer-led test against a staging environment; Redwood will provide ephemeral access tokens and an agreed test window. Third-party vendor tests require a mutual non-disclosure and an MRA executed prior to testing.

I tried to balance Vitria's ask for visibility with Redwood's operational constraints. If Vitria needs a shorter turnaround for specific artifacts we can scope a paid compliance add-on.

On the triage call: please be ready to confirm (a) whether Vitria accepts sampling frequency (twice per year cap), (b) whether the 14-day pen-test notice is workable, and (c) if procurement needs a DocuSign route for the MRA.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
Attachments: redline_snippets.docx (docx)

Following up with operational details we should include in the mutual action plan and order form appendix: 

- SOC 2 artifacts: we will provide CSV extracts of control mappings, auditor letter (redacted where necessary), and a sample of system logs for the scoped assertions. Delivery target: within 7 business days of the scheduled quarterly bundle (we agreed 10 business days in email thread; legal can keep the 10-day SLA, ops will aim for 7).

- Pen-test staging: we will provide an isolated staging endpoint, ephemeral credentials, and a contact list for the war room. We will confirm a no-change freeze for the agreed window and record any changes in a post-test runbook.

- Evidence redaction: any PII or customer metadata will be redacted before artifacts are shared; legal should keep language that allows reasonable sampling while protecting tenant data.

Alice — if this aligns with Vitria's compliance team, Ben and I can publish the mutual action plan into the deal workspace (HubSpot ID HS-34921) and Laura can push the redline into the order form appendix.
